text:
emily: Quick thread 10min 1: I'm updating the Devcontainer + Hello quickstart. Recurring problems: inline API_KEY in Node sample, no devcontainer ports/forwarding note, and our GH Actions example shows secrets inline. Planning a small PR to switch samples to DefaultCredentials, add devcontainer.json portForward, and a tiny CI snippet. Anyone want to review?
ton y: I can take the code review. Please also add a short note about client-side vs server-side token usage (don't expose tokens to browser).
emily: Good call. I'll add a `Server vs Browser` note and show a safe server snippet. Also replacing `const API_KEY = 'sk_...'` with DefaultCredentials: 
```js
// prefer DefaultCredentials: env -> file -> secrets
const creds = await DefaultCredentials.load();
const client = new RedwoodClient({ auth: creds });
```
harpreet: For devcontainer, add `forwardPorts` and a task to run the sample. Example devcontainer.json: 
```json
{
  "name": "Hello Dev",
  "forwardPorts": [3000],
  "postCreateCommand": "npm ci && npm run build"
}
```
Note: call out that 3000 is the app port in the quickstart.
emily: I'll add that and a short VS Code tip about the "Open in Container" command. Also planning to change Docker Compose example to avoid mounting secrets into the image and instead show an env_file reference.
ton y: For GH Actions, please show how to inject the secret without printing it: 
```yaml
- name: Set REDWOOD_API_TOKEN
  run: echo "REDWOOD_API_TOKEN=${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_TOKEN }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
- run: npm ci && npm run test
```
Add a :no_entry_sign: warning: "Never echo secrets to logs."
sam: Small wording request: in the Server vs Browser section show a diff with short examples. e.g.: 
Server:
```js
// server-only: safe to use env
const client = new RedwoodClient({ auth: process.env.REDWOOD_API_TOKEN });
```
Browser:
```js
// client: never put token in client bundle. Use server proxy instead.
fetch('/api/proxy')
```
harpreet: Also add a 1-line migration hint for SDK v5 -> v6 (we get questions): update package, replace `new Client(opts)` with `new RedwoodClient({ auth })` and check `getToken()` rename. Link to changelog.
emily: Good. I'll include a tiny Migration section with that one-liner and link. CI: I'll open a draft PR with changes and samples.
ci-bot: Draft PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/881-devcontainer-quickstart-auth-ci-smoke 1checks: markdown-lint, link-check, sample-runner queued.
ton y: I'll run the samples locally after CI. Quick UX ask: add an explicit health endpoint check in the devcontainer task that waits for the server to be ready before opening preview. Something like `npx wait-on http://localhost:3000/health`
emily: Adding `wait-on` to the postCreateCommand. Also replacing any `console.log(process.env.REDWOOD_API_TOKEN)` in samples with a red admonition and an example of secure read-from-env.
sam: I'll do a quick copyedit on the PR once the preview is up. If markdown-lint complains about long code fence language, change to proper fence names.
ci-bot: PR #881 1: link-check failed (old redirect to /guides/auth).
emily: Fixed redirect in a follow-up commit, pushing now.
ci-bot: PR #881 1: link-check passed. markdown-lint passed. sample-runner: success.
emily: Thanks all. If sam approves I'll merge and add a short CHANGELOG line: "devcontainer quickstart: auth snippet safety, devcontainer ports, CI secret example, health check". Planning to land in today's docs patch. :tada:
